Live Analysis walkthrough

Structured queries and local MCP

On this page

  2. MCP configuration

Available starting with v0.2.0. The published v0.1.0 binaries do not contain these modes.

The same typed analysis interface serves one-shot JSON queries and a local stdio MCP process. It reads a selected x86-64 ELF or supported thin Mach-O; it does not execute that file. Existing human CLI commands keep their output format.

JSON CLI

xref -b app.elf query '{"operation":"info"}'
xref -b app.elf query '{"operation":"strings","text":"needle"}'
xref -b app.elf query '{"operation":"refs","address":"0x1200"}'
xref -b app.elf query '{"operation":"calls","address":"0x1000"}'
xref -b app.elf query '{"operation":"slice","address":"0x1000","to":"0x1007"}'

These are request-shape examples; replace addresses with evidence returned for your input. Each invocation writes one JSON response and exits nonzero for an application error. Parse error before consuming data.

Every response includes schema_version: 1, tool/package version, optional build revision, image identity, operation, data/error, warnings and pagination. Image identity contains the SHA-256 of the exact loaded file bytes, size, format, architecture and the image base used for RVAs: the lowest load-segment VA for ELF, or __TEXT.vmaddr for supported Mach-O. Addresses are hexadecimal strings, preserving all 64 bits in JSON clients. They are static image virtual addresses; no runtime ASLR slide is inferred.

MCP configuration

Start one process for one image:

xref -b app.elf mcp

For a client using the common mcpServers configuration shape:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "xref": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/xref",
      "args": ["-b", "/absolute/path/to/app.elf", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}

The server advertises the 2025-11-25 protocol and its initialization lifecycle: initialize, notifications/initialized, then tool requests. It exposes one read-only tool, xref_query, with generated input/output schemas. Its arguments wrap the same query object used by the CLI:

{"name":"xref_query","arguments":{"request":{"operation":"info"}}}

Analysis responses appear in structuredContent and as serialized JSON in a text content block. Application failures set isError: true; malformed MCP requests use JSON-RPC errors. Stdout carries only protocol frames; diagnostics go to stderr. The current SDK's legacy client and its automatic fallback from modern discovery are covered by a real subprocess integration test. A discovery-only 2026-07-28 lifecycle is not implemented in this first version.

The image is an immutable snapshot loaded once at startup. File changes do not silently replace it; restart the process to select new bytes. Tool arguments cannot open other filesystem paths. Runtime dependencies do not include an async runtime or MCP SDK; those are used only by the reference-client tests.

Opt-in live process inspection (--allow-live-pid)

By default, xref -b app.elf mcp is strictly static and exposes only xref_query. On Linux x86-64, you can explicitly bind the MCP server to one verified running process at startup:

xref -b app.elf mcp --allow-live-pid 12345

When --allow-live-pid <PID> is provided:

  • Startup verifies PID != 0, /proc/<pid>/stat starttime_ticks, /proc/<pid>/exe (dev, ino), and binary identity (verified_build_id or verified_sha256 against -b app.elf). Any mismatch or dead PID aborts startup before emitting protocol frames.
  • tools/list exposes a second tool, xref_live (readOnlyHint: false, destructiveHint: false, idempotentHint: false, openWorldHint: false), wrapping LiveQuery (maps, resolve, memscan, probe, watch):
{"name":"xref_live","arguments":{"request":{"operation":"maps"}}}
{"name":"xref_live","arguments":{"request":{"operation":"resolve","addresses":["0x555555555140"]}}}
{"name":"xref_live","arguments":{"request":{"operation":"memscan","values":["0x1122334455667788"],"max_hits":16,"timeout_ms":2000}}}
{"name":"xref_live","arguments":{"request":{"operation":"probe","addresses":["0x1140"],"callers":true,"regs":true,"duration_ms":1000}}}
{"name":"xref_live","arguments":{"request":{"operation":"watch","addresses":["0x7f0000001000"],"follow":["ptr_slot=0x7f0000002000,offset=16"],"duration_ms":1000}}}
{"name":"xref_live","arguments":{"request":{"operation":"profile","duration_ms":1000,"max_events":4096}}}
  • Tool arguments cannot supply pid, bin, or force_bin (deny_unknown_fields). Every xref_live call re-checks the pinned (pid, starttime_ticks, exe_dev_ino) identity and fails with error.code == "process_exited" or "process_changed" if the target process exited or was replaced.
  • At most one xref_live request runs at a time (busy on concurrent live calls), with MCP caps of duration_ms / timeout_ms <= 5000, max_hits <= 64, max_events <= 4096, and MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (64 KiB). See Linux live analysis for full L1–L4 semantics and caveats.
  • The Live Analysis walkthrough shows the same operations as recorded CLI runs against a stripped fixture process.

Operations

OperationRequired fieldsResult
infononeCounts of unwind ranges, segments, symbols, imports and pointers.
stringstextSorted virtual addresses of matching byte sequences.
refsaddressRIP-relative memory references and recognized one-hop pointer slots. Optional back is 0..64 bytes. Direct branch operands are excluded.
functionaddressCovering unwind range, RVA, name hint and provenance.
callsaddressInstruction addresses, call kinds and known targets; unresolved indirect branches are reported separately.
callersaddressKnown reverse call sites, caller FDEs and unresolved-edge counts.
call_contextaddress, call_siteConservative argument-register candidates, guards and instruction evidence.
investigaterequestBounded string/function discovery, graph traversal and an explicitly selected slice.
field_originrequestEntry-relative field accesses, address versus loaded-value register origins and bounded one-hop callee evidence.
asmaddressInstruction bytes, addresses/RVAs, decoder validity and direct reference evidence.
caddressPseudo-C from the existing renderer. Optional fields and keep_gotos.
sliceaddress, to or to_fieldA backward slice to an instruction, call, or memory field (+0x10 of rax@0xVA). Optional fields and keep_gotos.

Per-function operations require a file-backed .eh_frame FDE range. Its range_origin is eh_frame_fde: this is evidence for an unwind range, not proof of a complete source-level function. This initial API does not expose the human CLI's synthetic-span fallback. The loader requires parseable DWARF unwind records. See Mach-O inputs for bases, linkage and partial coverage. Non-x86-64, big-endian and unsupported container variants are rejected.

Bounded investigations compose this workflow into discovery and explicit selection, retaining alternative call sites and intermediate evidence.

Field-origin investigations distinguish base/address/value relationships and retain the memory instructions observed in known callees.

For individual queries, search the string, follow returned reference rows to a function, inspect its calls/assembly, then slice to the selected call-site instruction address. Use calls[].address for an exact site; a callee target address may appear at multiple call sites. slice.to otherwise uses the existing CLI matching rules for names/text/addresses. Inspect all pages and resolve multiple candidates explicitly.

Budgets, continuation and errors

  • Images: at most 256 MiB of input bytes.
  • Item pages: "page":{"offset":0,"limit":20}, limit 1..100, offset at most
    1. Continue with page.next_offset using the same operation/arguments and image identity. Lists are sorted by VA or instruction address. At the maximum offset, remaining results produce pagination_window_exhausted with complete: false and no next offset; narrow the query instead of receiving an unusable continuation token.
  • Text pages: "page":{"offset":0,"limit":8192}, limit 4..16384 UTF-8 bytes. Use the returned byte offset; arbitrary offsets inside a code point are rejected. A partial text payload has fragment: true and an explicit warning. Reassemble pages before treating it as the complete renderer output.
  • Assembly/call ranges: at most 1 MiB. Pseudo-C/slices: at most 32 KiB of machine code and 2 MiB of generated text.
  • Canonical analysis JSON: at most 64 KiB. Oversized results return response_too_large; reduce the page limit. The auxiliary pointer-slot list is capped at 100 with a truncation flag; reference rows remain paginated.
  • Stdio input frames: 64 KiB; oversized frames are drained through the next newline before processing resumes. Output frames: 256 KiB, including protocol metadata and the compatibility text block.
  • At most two analysis requests run at once. Additional requests get busy; there is no unbounded work queue. IDs of active requests cannot be reused.

notifications/cancelled signals a matching active query without producing a notification response. Cancellation is cooperative: scans poll between chunks or instructions, while existing decompilation/slicing phases finish before the next check. A cancelled worker retains its concurrency slot until it ends. EOF cancels remaining requests and joins their workers. This is not a hard preemptive CPU or memory limit for the existing analysis algorithms.

Errors distinguish invalid requests/addresses/pages, unsupported or unreadable images, missing/invalid unwind ranges, excessive function/output sizes, missing slice targets and cancellation. Check warning codes: pseudo-C, field hints and slices remain heuristic reconstructions. No unknown value is promoted to a recovered source fact by the transport.

Verification

Offline stack symbolization is also available through xref_query with operation: "symbolize". It accepts bounded inline stacks and the selected image's runtime base, never an arbitrary filename or PID. See offline stacks and observed edges for request examples, mapping assumptions and limits. The same guide distinguishes native-stack integration fixtures from optional actual kernel perf recording.

tests/mcp.rs compiles a small redistributable Rust fixture as a stripped ELF, then uses the official Rust MCP SDK as an actual child-process client. It checks image digest, tool discovery, the string-to-slice chain, instruction evidence, continuation, errors, and byte-for-byte CLI parity for pseudo-C and slices. Additional wire tests check malformed/oversized frames, initialization, notifications, stdout framing, shutdown and unsupported images.

The test logs startup-to-initialization, the query sequence through the slice, and total verification time separately. These are observations for one small fixture, not general performance comparisons. CI separately checks the runtime at the declared Rust 1.88 minimum.
